intro_h2: Custom Kitchen Remodeling in Los Angeles County
intro: The kitchen is the hardest-working room in the house and the one that returns the most value when it's done right. Palm Crest Builders designs and builds custom kitchens across Los Angeles County — from cabinet-and-counter refreshes to full layout changes with removed walls and new islands. As a licensed general contractor we manage cabinetry, countertops, plumbing, electrical, lighting, flooring, and finish carpentry as one coordinated project, so your kitchen is beautiful, functional, and built to code.
benefits: Custom and semi-custom cabinetry, islands, and pantry storage
Quartz, granite, and natural-stone countertops with expert fabrication
Layout changes — wall removals, relocated sinks, and added islands
Updated electrical, lighting, plumbing, and ventilation to current code
Durable flooring, tile backsplashes, and finish carpentry
One licensed team managing every trade — CA Class B contractor

body_extra.heading: How Much Does a Kitchen Remodel Cost in LA?
body_extra.text: In the Los Angeles market, a mid-range kitchen remodel typically runs from the mid-five figures for a cabinet-and-counter refresh to six figures for a full layout change with custom cabinetry, structural work, and high-end appliances. The biggest cost drivers are cabinetry, countertops, whether you move plumbing or walls, and appliance selection. Every estimate we provide is written and itemized so you can see exactly where your budget goes.

faqs.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?
faqs.a: Most kitchens take 4–8 weeks of on-site work once materials arrive. Custom cabinetry and stone often have a 4–8 week lead time, which we order early.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remodel my kitchen?
faqs.a: Cosmetic swaps usually don't, but moving plumbing, gas, electrical, or walls does. We pull all required permits and schedule inspections for you.

faqs.q: Can you remove a wall to open up my kitchen?
faqs.a: Yes. We assess whether it's load-bearing, engineer a beam if needed, pull the permit, and build it properly — a common and popular upgrade.
